newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai B index ends down on Heilongjiang.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai B index ends down on Heilongjiang.

text.p: Shanghai's B share index ended down on Monday, dampened by poor performance of blue-chip Heilongjiang Electric Power after it posted lower-than-expected 1996 results, brokers said.
The B index edged down 0.018 points or 0.03 percent to 70.88 points on volume of 20.151 million shares worth $10.448 million.
Heilongjiang fell $0.036 or 2.63 percent to $0.740 after it proposed a 0.17325 yuan per share dividend for B share holders based on its 1996 net profit of 124.92 million yuan.

Brokers said falls of Heilongjiang Electric Power and losses on the A share market later in the session erased early gains, but active institutional support buying in real estate developer Shanghai Lujiazui Finance and Trade Zone Development prevented the market from further losses.

"Losses on the A share market triggered some profit-taking on the B share market in the afternoon," said one broker. "But most investors held their positions because of strong institutional support for Lujiazui."
Shanghai Lujiazui traded the most and became the star on institutional buying, rising $0.026 or 2.78 percent to $0.960 on volume of 3.6 million shares.
Another broker said technical charts showed the market had entered into a correction period. "The index will linger around 70 points in the short term if there is no negative market-moving news."
Of 43 B shares, 42 traded, 22 down, seven flat and 13 up.
Textile machinery maker Shangha Erfangji was the biggest loser on expectations of poor 1996 results, slipping $0.010 or 5.55 percent to $0.170 on volume of 945,600 shares.
Shanghai A shares ended up, but off intraday highs on profit-taking, triggered by investor concerns over possible government intervention to cool down the market, brokers said.
The index gained 4.477 points or 0.37 percent to 1,217.230 points on volume of 977.8 million shares worth 11.9 billion yuan.
The SSE30 index rose 20.178 points or 0.63 percent to 3,235.234 points.
Tientsin Marine Shipping was the star on talk about its dividend plans, surging 1.25 yuan or 10.01 percent to 13.73 on volume of 2.8 million shares.
